facts.statement: Acantholipan was a herbivorous nodosaurid dinosaur that lived in Mexico during the early Santonian age of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Acantholipan is a genus of herbivorous nodosaurid dinosaur from Mexico from the early Santonian age of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: A partial skeleton of Acantholipan was first described in 2011 from fossils found at Los Primos near San Miguel in Coahuila, Mexico.
facts.quote: A partial skeleton excavated at Los Primos near San Miguel in Coahuila, was described in 2011.

facts.statement: The type species Acantholipan gonzalezi was formally named by Rivera-Sylva and colleagues in 2018.
facts.quote: In 2018, the type species Acantholipan gonzalezi was named by Rivera-Sylva et al.

facts.statement: The specific name gonzalezi honors Mexican paleontologist Arturo Homero González-González, who chaired the Museo del Desierto.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the Mexican paleontologist Arturo Homero González-González, the chairman of the Museo del Desierto at Saltillo.

facts.statement: Acantholipan is the first ankylosaurian species to be named from Mexico.
facts.quote: Acantholipan is the first ankylosaurian species named from Mexico.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen CPC 272 was found in a marine layer of the Pen Formation alongside another nodosaur and dates to the Santonian.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, CPC 272, was found alongside another nodosaur, CPC 273, in a marine layer of the Pen Formation and dates from the Santonian.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton lacking the skull, including vertebrae, a rib fragment, limb bones, and a spike-like osteoderm likely from the posterior thorax.
facts.quote: It consists of partial skeleton lacking the skull. Its remains include a back vertebra, a tail vertebra, a piece of a rib, the underside of the left humerus, an upper left ulna, the underside of the left femur and a spike-like osteoderm probably from the posterior thorax.

facts.statement: Acantholipan lived during the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 83 million years ago, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico durante el Santoniense, hace aproximadamente 83 millones de años en lo que es hoy América del Norte.

facts.statement: Fossils of Acantholipan were found in marine strata of the Pen Formation in Coahuila, Mexico, and consist only of postcranial material.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles se encontraron en Coahuila, México, en estratos marinos de la Formación Pen, los cuales solo consisten en material postcraneal.

facts.statement: Acantholipan belongs to the subfamily Nodosaurinae and is the sister taxon to Nodosaurus.
facts.quote: Acantholipan belongs to the Nodosaurinae and is the sister taxon to Nodosaurus.

facts.statement: Acantholipan is classified within the family Nodosauridae.
Acantholipan possessed tall, spine-shaped osteoderms located above the hips.
facts.quote: Se sabe que el Acantholipan gonzalezi poseía osteodermos altos en forma de púas encima de la cadera.

facts.statement: Acantholipan is distinguished from other nodosaurids by a combination of features including a prominent, tapered ulna and a conical lateral thoracic osteoderm with an oval longitudinal section.
facts.quote: Se distingue de las demás especies de nodosáuridos debido a la siguiente combinación de características, ulna con un proceso anterolateral prominente, ahusado y truncado proximalmente, triangular en vista lateral, osteodermo lateral torácico cónico y ligeramente caudal con una sección longitudinal ovalada y surcos vasculares en la cara lateral solamente.

facts.statement: The time range for Acantholipan is recorded as the Campanian, spanning from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus name Acantholipan combines the Greek word for 'spine' with the Spanish name for the Lépai-Ndé, a tribe of Apache people living near the fossil site.
rejected.quote: The generic name combines a Greek akanthos, 'spine', with lipán, the usual Spanish designation of the Lépai-Ndé, the 'Gray People', a tribe of the Apache inhabiting the area of the find.
